Can you please comment on what additional powers, perhaps extraordinary powers, were given to the presidential council, and generally comment on its function and importance.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. The House of Deputies, pursuant to Article 8(a), follows and coordinates political, strategic and in defence affairs, and in emergency situations discharges the rights and duties of the presidents of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. These last things fall out of line with other parliamentary and systems, or, rather, constitutional systems in other European parliamentary systems. Namely, if we take the Republic of Croatia as an example, or the Republic of Slovenia. When the president of the republic is enabled to discharge his functions, then, both in Slovenia and in Croatia, these functions may be discharged by the president of the parliament, that is of the High Chamber. That is in emergency situations the Chamber of Deputies discharges the rights and duties of the president of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, and these powers are very, very broad. And, as I said, goes beyond the usual such powers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Dr. Ribicic, returning to the status of Herceg-Bosna with regard to Croatia. Your footnote, 140 in your paper, which is translated into English in your paper, bears a comment by Mate Boban. And I wonder if you could comment on that footnote, please. If it would facilitate for the Court, we also have taken copies from the original document of Z2717, which has been previously tendered, but it might help, just for looking at the full quote.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This is a fragment of Mate Boban's intervention or, rather, one of the introductory speeches at a meeting in Zagreb held on the 27th of December '91. Mate Boban said, and I shall quote only the last part of his statement, and he says that this area, that is of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, should be proclaimed an independent Croat territory and joined to the state of Croatia, but at a time and at the moment when the Croatian top leadership, which our people applies for trust in, decides that the right moment had come. The end of the quotation. So this is a quotation which shows that, in Mate Boban's view, and at that moment, he was discharging the functions of the president of the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, hat the motive for the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna rested with the joining -- its integration with the territory of the Republic of Croatia, and that the Croatian leadership, that is the agencies of the Republic of Croatia, will decide that the right moment has come. So this was an interpretation by Mr. Boban. Perhaps more important is the decision read at the same meeting by the secretary of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Mr. Ignac Kostroman. That decision was taken on the 23rd of December, '91, and read: "The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna confirms once again the aspiration of whole Croat people of Herceg-Bosna as expressed on the 18th, 12th '91 at Grude, which passed a historic decision on the establishment of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, constituting the legal framework, the legal basis for the integration of new territories with the Republic of Croatia." So, this was a decision of an extended meeting of the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, explicitly stating that the establishment of that community served as the legal basis for the integration of this territory with the neighbouring Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Dr. Ribicic, your footnote 204, which is the very last footnote of your paper, quotes Hrvoje Sarinic. The translation of the quote is available, because it is in the translated footnote. The actual original document from Mr. Sarinic's book has been labelled as Z2811.1. If the Court would simply like to see what the nature of the source is. But I ask you to comment on that footnote. And please indicate who Hrvoje Sarinic was, and what, if anything, his role may have been in the aspects of the division of Bosnia, particularly with Karadjordjevo?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: According to the book quoted in this footnote, and that is Hrvoje Sarinic's book, "All my secret negotiations with Slobodan Milosevic between 1993 and 1995," Mr. Sarinic was a man picked out by Mr. Slobodan Milosevic, picked out by selected -- excuse me. Selected by Dr. Tudjman to establish the first contacts with Mr. Slobodan Milosevic. And the whole book is about his encounters with Milosevic. And this fragment refers to Mr. Slobodan Milosevic's attitude toward the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. So this is not the opinion of the author of the book, but, rather, his interpretation of Mr. Milosevic's words, who says that with Republika Srpska he has solved 90 percent of the Serb national question, and adds, quoting, "In the same way that Tudjman resolved the national issue of Croatia with Herceg-Bosna, I have nothing against a union of three peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina, but it cannot last long, because nobody wants that union." This is important, because the acceptance of the union of three sovereign republics, and even those compromised solutions which were arrived at later, can all be viewed as a provisional solution which is, of necessity, short-lived. And thus Serbia and, in Slobodan Milosevic's view, in the long run Croatia will, like Serbia, achieve its long-term interest and manage to partition Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Just to clarify, this is Hrvoje Sarinic, who was the chef de cabinet of President Tudjman; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Dr. Tudjman, with Herceg-Bosna having, as you have indicated in your paper, done almost everything de jure to divorce itself from Bosnia and Herzegovina, and to integrate into Croatia, based on your analysis that you have referred to at the very beginning of your testimony, using your two-storey or two-level approach, can you conclude, or do you have any conclusions as to whether or not the effective governance, the aspect of effective governance, one of the essential components of statehood was met, where it has been demonstrated that the policies carried out by Herceg-Bosna, with the policies of another sovereign, that is the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: When I began my testimony, I said that my analysis was based on normative acts adopted by the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. And it was only later that I read material and testimonies about the so-called second storey about Herceg-Bosna, from which the subordination of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna to the neighbouring state transpires. I must say that the record of the meeting held in Belgrade on the 27th December, '91 --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was that Belgrade or Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Zagreb. Zagreb. I'm sorry. Sorry, the meeting was in Zagreb. So the 27th December '91, in Zagreb. That document has helped me decisively to forming my view that this second storey became -- has become more important than the first one. All that I said about the elements which a state must comply with, must have, if it is to be considered an independent and sovereign state, and especially the fourth component, and that is direct subordination to international law, all this loses its significance when we are confronted with the truth. That at some political meetings, instructions were issued and guidelines were issued, which were then translated into life in subsequent -- in subsequently adopted regulations of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And the particular cogent parts of the document to which you are referring, have been reinforced by other documents and other sources of information, which you have received?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The testimony I feel to be very significant coming from individuals who had direct, high positions, held high positions in the HDZ of Croatia and the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And I have already mentioned two of them, two names, Mr. Stipe Mesic is one, and Mr. Kljuic the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And your reference to Mr. Mesic is from newspaper articles; that is correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned both of these individuals on the basis of the newspaper article that appeared, although in the case of Mr. Stjepan Kljuic, this newspaper article taken from Feral Tribune relates to the testimony before this Tribunal in The Hague. And the same is true for Mesic's interview in the Globus newspaper. So these are both newspaper articles, but relate to their testimony before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. At this time, nothing further.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Dr. Ribicic, good afternoon. My name is Steven Sayers --

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: -- and I am one of the attorneys representing Mr. Kordic. The meeting that you referred to during a large part of your testimony today, the meeting that occurred on December the 27th, 1991, in Zagreb, that was actually three months before the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was even founded; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: No, that meeting took place on the 27th of December, 1991, while the forming -- while the formation of the community of Herceg-Bosna was on the 18th of February, the same year. November the same year. So that was about 40 days later, after the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Dr. Ribicic, I don't know whether you misheard me, but let me repeat my question. Isn't it true that the meeting that you referred to in Zagreb in December of 1991 occurred three months before the foundation of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which I believe was founded on March the 6th, 1992. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I thought you were speaking about the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. But it is not true that the Republic of Herceg-Bosna -- Herceg-Bosna was formed at the time you mentioned. So the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was formed, was established on the 18th of November, 1991. The Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna was formed much later, that is to say on the 28th of August, 1993, not in the spring of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Dr. Ribicic, do you know when the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina as an independent country was founded; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was one of the republics of the former Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: When did it become independent and change its status from that of a Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to becoming the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina became an independent and autonomous state with the disintegration of the former Yugoslav Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me see if I can help you, sir. Let me show you a document that I'd like to have marked as the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D180/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, sir, isn't it true that on March the 6th, 1992, following the referendum on the question of independence, the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was founded?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And that, sir, is about three months after the December 1991 meeting in Zagreb, about which we've heard so much today; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So this Zagreb meeting that you've talked about occurred in a context where the independent Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina didn't even exist; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: You could put it that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, isn't it true, sir, that no law or decree was ever passed in the HZ HB or HR HB that ever limited the voting rights of any persons or any groups, that you've seen?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: No, there are no such express provisions limiting this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Very well. Now, there are equally no restrictions on the number of political parties that can exist either in the HZ HB or the HR HB; would you agree with that, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: That is correct, but those parties could not be represented in the organs of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna because, by virtue of its name and the way in which it was formed, it was exclusively reserved for Croatian representatives; that is to say, the representatives of the Croatian people, which is expressly stipulated in the organs of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, we'll look at that in just a minute as we go through some of the decrees. Just for your information, Dr. Ribicic, and for the Trial Chamber's information, here's what I would propose to do: I have prepared three volumes; two of them are pretty short, one of them is a little longer. The first volume is the constitutive documents of the HZ HB; the second volume are documents relating to the HVO; the third volume of documents relates to the founding and functioning of the HR HB, which was founded, as you say, on the 28th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: With the Trial Chamber's permission, I would like to distribute those right now. I believe copies have already been given to the Prosecution and to counsel for Mr. Cerkez, and to the translators, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It looks like a daunting amount of paperwork, Dr. Ribicic, but actually we're going to touch very lightly on some of these documents, and what I propose to do is to go through them in a chronological fashion so that everybody has a good sense of how these --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you slow down, Mr. Sayers, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: -- everyone has a good sense of how these institutions evolved and what they did, and equally important, who performed what function in each of these institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: My apologies to the Trial Chamber for inundating it with yet more paperwork, but each of these volumes is arranged chronologically and I think that you will see that we can go through the documents in fairly short order and in, hopefully, a logical way. If we can get the Defence exhibit numbers, please. The HZ HB first, the HVO second, and HR HB third.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If the witness could be given the three volumes, that would be helpful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Ribicic, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the HZ HB, was founded the same day or the day after the fall of Vukovar in the Republic of Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That was on November the 18th, 1991, as you said; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If you would turn, sir, to the first volume, the one that says "HZ HB" on the spine, one of the smaller volumes. Yes, that's right, the one beneath that, I think. There we go, that's the one. You were shown a document that was marked Exhibit Z27.2, and it's a founding decision. There are two versions of it, but in the first version, you were also read the following, and it's at page 1649, up on the top right-hand corner for the Trial Chamber's reference, it says: "We Croats of Bosnia-Herzegovina, through our Croatian Democratic Union and through our elected government representatives in this Republic, have supported a sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina, but we have always emphasised that we shall do so only until others start dividing Bosnia-Herzegovina." That was part of the founding decision, wasn't it, Dr. Ribicic?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But once again, as we know, this was before the independent Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina had actually been founded; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, but Bosnia-Herzegovina as a republic existed previously, so there wasn't a legal void at that particular time. Quite clearly, it no longer existed in the federal form that Yugoslavia existed, but Bosnia-Herzegovina existed with its constitutional and legal order.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Quite so, sir. But if you take a look at Article 5 of the November the 18th, 1991 decision, the HZ HB stated that it would respect the democratically elected government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina "as long as Bosnia-Herzegovina remains an independent state in relation to former or any future Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You'd have to agree, sir, wouldn't you, that as of the date that the HZ HB was founded, in November of 1991, the future of Bosnia-Herzegovina and its constituent peoples was absolutely up in the air, it was a thing that was unknown, uncertain; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, just taking a look, sir, at the constitutive document, which is tab 1 of this volume, Article 7 of this document stated that the "Supreme authority of the Community shall be the Presidency which comprises the most senior representatives of the Croatian people in the municipal authority or Presidents of the Croatian Democratic Union Municipal Boards"; right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You gave some testimony about the presidency, and I think we'll see that the concept evolves, but the presidency initially consisted, therefore, of at least 30 individuals, did it not? At least one representative from each of the component municipalities.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Then it was the presidency, this agglomeration of at least 30 representatives, who would proceed to elect the president, two deputy-presidents, and a secretary; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In this early document, sir, there's no -- actually, let me rephrase the question. In this early document, it's a fairly embryonic, evolutionary, dare we say, rather simple document that does not actually provide for a legislature, does it?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. The legislature was this component of representatives from the 30 municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If we're going to apply governmental analogies to this particular document, Dr. Ribicic, would you agree that the supreme authority would mean that the presidency was endowed with basically legislative, executive, and administrative power; right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Right, and I said that in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes. All mixed and jumbled together in one entity; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You would agree with me, sir, that over the ensuing years, those functions gradually became separate and distinct; the legislative power evolved into a separately identifiable set of provisions, the same was true of the executive authority, and the same was true of the administrative authority; wouldn't you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: That's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Indeed, and I'm sure you've seen these documents, and if you haven't, we'll take a look at them as we go through this, initially, the military aspects of the community and the civilian aspects of the community, if we are to use those two terms, they were also mixed together, weren't they? In other words, there was no separation of military and civilian functions; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But as the embryonic community evolved, the civilian functions did separate out from the military functions, didn't they, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I didn't deal with that question so much, but that is what happened. I focused on the development of the organs of legislation and the executive and administrative ones and functions, and to a lesser extent, the separation between the civilian and military power and authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and we will go through that in a little bit more detail at the appropriate time, as we proceed through these documents chronologically. But just starting out in November of 1991, it's true that Mr. Boban was elected the president of the presidency; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That Mr. Kordic and Mr. Bozo Rajic were elected deputy-presidents of the presidency; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And, finally, Mr. Ignac Kostroman was elected the secretary of the presidency; yes?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, I think you said that the powers and functions of this nascent presidency, if you like, were not specifically defined in the constitutive documents, the early ones; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. The next period I would like to draw your attention to is April the 8th of 1992, the date that the HVO was actually founded. The HVO was founded on the same day that the presidency of the republic, sir, issued a declaration of an imminent threat of war; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It's also correct that this new republic was born under the imminent threat of war, and that imminent threat came to fruition within weeks of the founding of the republic, when Neum was attacked, Mostar was attacked, and ultimately when Sarajevo was surrounded and besieged by the assembled forces of the Bosnian Serb Army; that's accurate to say, is it not?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: It is. The defence from the aggression is one of the causes or one of the reasons for the establishment of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I would just draw the Trial Chamber's attention to Exhibit D17.1/1, which is the decree declaring an imminent threat of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It was Mr. Boban, sir, that actually signed the decision to create the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council, in Mostar on April the 8th, was it not?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, he signed it as the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and also as the president of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. If you would turn, sir, to tab 1 of the thicker volume of documents, you'll see that there is a copy of that decision. I have tried in each case to put the Croatian original at the back of the exhibit, sir, and the English translation at the front. As you can see, Mr. Boban signs as president of the HVO and HZ HB; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You gave some testimony earlier this morning to the effect that the HVO was established as the supreme defence body of the Croatian people in the HZ HB, and we can see that from Article 1; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is the organ with executive powers, and I compared that to the function of government.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But, sir, Article 2 of this decision provides that its objective is not only to defend the sovereignty of territories in the HZ HB and to protect the Croatian people, but it also goes on to say, "as well as other peoples in this community attacked by an aggressor," doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that is true, and I quote this in expounding my position, and the fact is that for the first time, that is to say, on the 8th of April, 1992, for the first time, we have this particular formulation appearing. But this formulation did not satisfy some, shall I say, normal constitutional and legal criteria for systems, and I'd like to draw your attention to the fact that here, the members of other nations, that is to say, other peoples, were placed as second rate. So we have a type of document before this particular document which speak of the defence of the Croatian people and Croatian historical territory, and here for the first time we see that they are there to defend other peoples in this community attacked by an aggressor. So I must caution that this particular formulation came in rather late in the day, and, secondly, that it was mentioned and brought up in a way where it places these other peoples in a second-rate position, or second class position. Thirdly, I would like to revert to my third warning, and that is it is one thing, what is set down on paper, in black and white, and quite another thing what is implemented in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Dr. Ribicic, there is no question that the HVO was founded in emergency wartime conditions, is there?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: No. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And it's not surprising, sir, that it took some time for the organisation of this body to, how shall we say, coalesce and mature; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: That is not in dispute either.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Okay, it is not. It is also not in dispute, Dr. Ribicic, that between the foundation of the HZ HB on November the 18th, 1991 and the creation of the HVO on April the 8th, 1992, the HZ HB did not adopt or pass one single act or decree; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: In the translation I heard that it did not pass any act or decree. Well, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, the only acts or decrees ever passed by the HZ HB, if you like, were passed through the HVO, weren't they, after April the 8th of 1992?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, before the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna enacted different, that is brought in different conclusions and decisions, and amended the decision to establish the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, it also enacted this decision on the formation of the HVO. And other decisions were made as well, including the decision as to who would be entrusted with the representation of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, that is to say the functionaries of the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and to Dr. Tudjman himself, as president of the Republic of Croatia and president of the HDZ of Croatia. And he was entrusted with representing Herceg-Bosna in international agreements.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, Dr. Ribicic, but the question was very simple, and it will help us get along and finish up with your testimony a lot more quickly if you just answer the question that's asked. The question was: The only acts or decrees ever passed by the HZ HB were passed through the HVO after April the 8th of 1992. And that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers. But you are telling your own story, and you just want me to say "yes," because all the questions have been written in such a way that they require a "yes" answer. But I thought it was the point of hearing the testimony, not for you to tell your own story and giving me the right just to say "yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Dr. Ribicic, it's the judges who control the proceedings here. If the questions are unfair, we will say so, and we'll stop them. Counsel is asking the questions, as he is entitled to. Now, if there is a "yes" or "no" answer, it would enable us to get on more quickly if would you give it, if what he is saying right or not. Don't trouble about his purpose. That doesn't matter. What we want is your evidence. If there are any questions which need clarification, then your counsel -- prosecuting counsel will have the opportunity of re-examining at the end of your evidence, and indeed the judges can ask for clarification. But we'll get along more quickly if you just answer "yes" or "no," if a question is capable of being answered in those terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Dr. Ribicic, please don't mistake my questions as demonstrating any lack of courtesy towards you. I don't intend that. If the questions that I ask you to agree with are not accurate, please feel free to disagree and tell us what the facts are upon which my error proceeds. And I'd appreciate that. Let's just go forward with respect to the HVO, and the evolutionary nature of this institution. As far as I could track it, sir, the next major stage in the coalescence of the HVO as a government body occurs on May the 15th of 1992, with the passage of a statutory decision on the temporary organisation of executive authority and administration in the territory of the HZ HB. And I think that you can find that at Tab 2 of the document. It's true, is it not, that the HVO, according to Article 2 of the document, was explicitly established as a temporary body in wartime?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And the intention was that the HVO would always give way to government containing traditional legislative, executive and administrative organs, once that could actually be done, once conditions in society permitted the establishment of such a regular government. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: You can't find that in this statutory decision. But it often happened that under wartime conditions some bodies emerge, and then they gradually develop and transfer their powers to some other bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You are aware that the HVO formally ceased to exist when its ministries were folded into the HR-HB government on September the 30th, 1993. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So you would agree that the HVO was initially established as a temporary regional government, established under emergency conditions in wartime, when the government itself, the central government, wasn't working, and that it was established, essentially, by force of necessity, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, now, that question involved an assumption, and it also involved a series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me see if I can break it down, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Rather than asking the witness whether he would agree, it may be simpler to ask him, if it was established as a temporary regional government, established under emergency conditions in wartime. In fact, I'll ask the witness that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Dr. Ribicic, you heard the question. What is the answer to that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: My answer is that one can refer to the HVO as a provisional government of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, but I do have some trouble with the term "regional government." From the point of view of the then Republic of Bosnia-Hercegovinia, that was not a regional community, that is a community founded in the republic's territory proper. But in view of its ambitions, to either become a republic within a new Bosnia-Herzegovina and federation, or join the neighbouring Republic of Croatia, in view of that, I could hardly agree with the term "regional government."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Very well, Dr. Ribicic. Let's go on to some more prosaic matters. Could I turn your attention to Article 7 of the temporary organisation statutory decision. It's true, is it not, that the HVO was to be comprised of a president, vice-presidents, without specifying a number, department heads, and other members; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And it's also true that the presidency of the HZ HB would appoint and dismiss other members at the proposal of the HVO president. Correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the proposal of the HVO president. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And as of this date, May the 15th, I believe, 1992, it was Mr. Boban who was performing double duty, if you like, as the president of the HVO and the president of the presidency of the HZ HB; is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And under Article 9 of this decision, the HVO president would be in charge of the work of the HVO, would be held accountable for it, and, amongst other things, the HVO president would sign all official HVO documents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, as we know, sir, from this statutory decision, you can see from Article 1 that the HVO is gradually evolving and now its set up as the supreme executive and administrative body in the territory of the HZ HB; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. But what it means is that the presidency, until the founding of the HVO, discharged those executive functions by and large through its president, the two vice-presidents and the secretary of the presidents, or the presidency. I agree that as of this moment, that is as of May 15th onward, some of these functions are transferred from the presidency to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And would you agree also that since we now have the HVO performing executive and administrative functions, you could reach a legitimate inference that the presidency of the HZ HB, as we've previously described it, 30-odd people or more, that body represented, if we are using the governmental analogy, the legislature of the community. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: As of the founding of the HVO onward, the presidency, and in July a formal decision was taken to this effect, it became the representative body. But until then, various functions, especially the executive functions, could not be discharged by the plenum, that is not all the 30 municipal mayors. And the principal powers, the principal duties, rested with the four officials, the president, the two vice-presidents, and the secretary of the presidency, because this presidency as a body did not meet often.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Without belabouring that point, as of this date, May the 15th of 1992, there is no question that the military components of the HVO and the civilian governmental components of it were still all mixed up into one, all jumbled up into one; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And, as I understand it, sir, there were to be six ministry or six departments, finance being one, defence being another, justice being another. Let's just confine our attention to those three. That's correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you are aware that Dr. Jadranka Prlic was appointed the head of the Department of Finance, initially, on May the 15th, 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: I am not sure. I did not see this. I never saw the document saying that Mr. Prlic headed the finance department. But it is quite true that there was six departments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me suggest to you that Mr. Prlic was indeed initially appointed the head of the Department of Finance and, for example, Dr. Zoran Buntic was appointed as the head of the Department of Justice and general administration. Does that ring a familiar bell, sir, or do you just not know that information?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: I do not know the staff, the personnel, the names of people who headed those departments. I only know of the names of these departments. And that is what I can comment on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just a matter of detail, sir. I don't think it's particularly important, and I believe I may have misspoken. Outline 11, the year 1993 is obviously in error. It should be 1992 we are talking about. Now, sir, the next document I'd like to draw your attention to is the next tab, Tab 3. This is a statutory decision on the municipal executive authority and municipal administrations. This decree, sir, was adopted just a week before the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, or just a month before, rather -- I'm sorry, one week before the republic issued a formal declaration that a state of actual war existed in the republic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, this statutory decision was taken on the 15th of March, '92.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And under Article 2, insofar as the municipal governmental authorities were concerned, each municipal HVO would consist of a president and other of its members who shall be appointed or dismissed by the HZ HB's HVO; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So just to use an example of relevance in this particular case. For the municipalities of Vitez and Busovaca, as of June the 13th, 1992, the president of the municipal HVO's in both of those cities would be appointed by the HVO in Mostar; is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, until that time the functions in the municipalities were discharged by municipal assemblies and their executive bodies. And the HVO then supplanted them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Proceeding chronologically along, sir. One week later, you are aware that the republic actually declared a state of war; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And just for the Trial Chamber's information, that document has already been marked as D17/1.2. Let me turn to two dates, sir, which I would suggest to you are watersheds in the evolution of the HVO and in the gradual separation of the military from the civilian functions in that organisation. And the first date is July the 3rd of 1992. You would agree with me, Dr. Ribicic, and you would tell the Trial Chamber, that that was the first date upon which any significant volume of decrees was passed, adopted by the HVO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. And the decision on the founding of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was amended then, and that was also when a number of documents were adopted, which were then published at a later date, that is in September.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, doctor. But there is no question that on July the 3rd, a very significant number of organisational, governmental steps, or quasi-governmental steps were taken for the first time by the HVO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right. A few examples would suffice. For example, taking over the materials of the JNA, a decree was passed to that effect; a decree on public enterprises; decrees dealing with primary and secondary education, things of that variety. Would you agree, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In addition, sir, there was the first of a number of decrees that dealt with criminal law, this one being the enforcement of the law on misdemeanours. If you turn to Tab 6 of this volume, you can see it. Would it be right, sir, that in order to be a judge in the HZ HB, according to Article 7 of this enforcement of the law on misdemeanours, one had merely to be a citizen of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: One of the other appointments made on July the 3rd, sir, was the appointment of Bruno Stojic to be the head of the Department of Defence. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: No. No. I don't know about these personnel matters, but I do believe it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sayers, I think that your cross-examination should really be limited to things that were covered by the examination-in-chief. This is the testimony of an expert about certain institutions, such as the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, but you are not going back into the history and go through all the text which had to do -- I mean, with various Croat public figures and things. We are talking -- this is the testimony about the institutional framework, what were the institutions, what were the relationships amongst them, and so on and so forth. And if you focus on that, that would be of great help to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will try to do precisely that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: This date, sir, July the 3rd, 1992, saw, for the first time, the adoption of rules on military discipline that govern the HVO military forces. And that can be found at Tab 9. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: One final question on this subject. If you take a look at Tab 4, sir, there is a decision made that the Narodni List becomes the Official Gazette of the HZ HB. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And it's true that that list, basically, published all of the official actions of the HVO and the HZ HB thereafter; is that correct? Or at least until, to be more accurate, at least until the establishment of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna in August of 1993?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, except that these decisions are published with delay. The first decisions were published only as late as September, not in November, when Herceg-Bosna was founded, nor later, nor even on the 3rd of July, when new decisions were taken. It was all published subsequently in the Official Gazette of Herceg-Bosna, that is the Narodni List.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I think we are agreed on that. Now, you averted to an amended decision relating to the constitution or the make-up of the HZ HB that occurred on July the 3rd of 1993. And if you take a look at the slim volume again, the one that says HZ HB on the spine. I put that under Tab 2.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. In the restated elaboration of the reasons for the establishment of this community, and this is a few months after the establishment of the independent Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, you can see in the prefatory language, at the end of the first paragraph, that one of the reasons is because "... at these difficult moments in their history, when the last communist army of Europe united with the Chetniks is endangering the existence of the Croatian people and the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina ..." and then it goes on to say that the HDZ, the Croatian Democratic Union, and Croats in Bosnia and Herzegovina have supported a sovereign Bosnia and Herzegovina. There was no question, sir, that Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina did support an independent Bosnia and Herzegovina; in fact, I believe of the people that voted, as we've seen from the first document that you were shown today, 99,44 percent of the people that elected to participate in the referendum voted in favour of the establishment of an independent Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: As for the outcome of the referendum, that is right. Evidently, people, and I mean members of all three ethnicities of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did vote for an integral and sovereign Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that was what the bodies of the Republic of Croatia were also advocating. But I cannot say that they were really doing it to defend the sovereignty and integrity of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I already said in my testimony today, there are a number of documents, some material that that was not the case. But this formulation about reasons, this writing about the reasons for the founding is better than the one founding the recent opinion behind the original decision of November 1991. Of course, it is hard for me to say whether this is a matter of tactics or a changed attitude towards Bosnia-Herzegovina. However, I do feel that it is rather a matter of tactics, in view of all the documents and testimonies already referred to today, when I said that, of course, in public we speak about our support to the sovereignty of Bosnia-Herzegovina and yet work against it or, rather, for its partitioning and annexation of that part of the territory to the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Doctor, could I turn your attention to Article 7 of this amended decision, and this effected a change in the governments of the HZ HB, did it not? I think you've said that.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It established, in effect, two separate organs of supreme executive power, or actually one organ of supreme executive power and one organ of legislative power. First, you see Article 7(1) deals with the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And that would be Mate Boban throughout the existence of the HZ HB, from this point forward; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, because as of that moment, Mate Boban became the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, whereas until that moment, he was the president of the presidency of that same community.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It's important to distinguish these two concepts. The presidency of the HZ HB basically lasted from the very date of the foundation of the Community until the foundation of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna; you'd agree with that, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And the president only existed as of July the 3rd, 1993 forward.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Until that moment, there was the presidency, but evidently not all the members of the presidency were in an equal manner, that is, discharged the function that was taken over by the president. One cannot say that until that moment, until the 3rd of July, this function was discharged by Mate Boban, as the president of the presidency, until he became the president of the Community. Of course, he was one, and presumably one of the most important members of the presidency. But it's quite evident that the two vice-presidents and the secretary of the presidency also played very important roles, whereas other members of the presidency simply attended its sessions from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But I think you say in your report, and I think that's right, Dr. Ribicic, that the functions of a vice-president of the presidency diminished in importance after July the 3rd of 1992, and that was because the presidency essentially became a legislature; in fact, Article 7 specifically says that; right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, for two reasons: because the presidency had grown into a legislative body and, secondly, because a new function was set up, that is, the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. From then on, formally speaking, from the point of view of the system, the vice-president of the presidency was merely the vice-president of the presidency of the legislative body, rather than the vice-president of a body which was discharging the functions of the head of state. But I also must say that there are documents which I know of and which show that some vice-presidents signed some documents as vice-presidents of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, even though this was later, that is, after the 3rd of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But as of July the 3rd of 1992, it's true, is it not, that the presidency became the legislative body of the HZ HB, and, indeed, the presidency was responsible for the appointment of executive and administrative bodies of authority in the HZ HB, and that's exactly what Article 8 says; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: That is correct. If we now compare the situation with the modern parliamentary systems in Europe, then we could say that the presidency played a stronger role than a parliament has in modern European parliamentary systems, in modern European states; that is, a lesser autonomy of the HVO than is the case with the governments of modern European states.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, the second date to which I want to draw your attention is October the 17th, 1992, and that's also a seminal date, at least from the Defence's perspective, in the development of the institutions of the HVO. One of the documents adopted on that date is the third document in that file that you have in front of you, sir. No, the one you've just put aside. Dr. Ribicic, the one -- yes. Tab number 3. This is the document that prescribes the code of practice on the work of the presidency of the HZ HB, and I think that you were shown a copy of this document that was marked Exhibit Z341.2A. Just a few questions that I have in connection with this, sir. Could you turn to Article 20.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, sir, that the position of vice-president of the presidency, as of this date, October the 17th, 1992, was essentially a position that was endowed with purely parliamentary powers; powers, for example, to limit individual addresses at sessions of the presidency, to deny the same person the right to speak repeatedly about the same issue, to interrupt an address, and things of that variety.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. These are functions normally discharged by the president of the parliament or the speaker of the parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Very well. Now, we can put aside this thin document because I'm finished with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's now 4, Mr. Sayers, I see. How much longer do you anticipate you will be?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I have a 56-page outline and I'm now at page 25, so we're making good progress, Your Honour. I would anticipate that we should be through -- it won't take longer than tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We've got another witness lined up; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. I think we've got witnesses to take us through tomorrow and Thursday. There may possibly be a short hiatus because of the time of arrival of one or more of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have to discuss the transcripts as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have tomorrow the pre-Defence conference; however, we will deal with the matter set out in the Rules. I think we arranged it for half past four. It may be convenient to deal with that at an appropriate moment during the afternoon, when we've finished some of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And possibly a short ex parte, if it's possible to organise one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, sooner rather than later because it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. How long do you anticipate that being?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes, I should think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, the most convenient time would be after everything else, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me hand something down to the registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: May it please the Court. We have an ex parte application as well that can we heard any time; I suspect it will take five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If it's a motion which you've sent in recently --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- there is an answer on its way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: I couldn't ask for more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Dr. Ribicic, I'm afraid we haven't finished your evidence, and so would you please come back tomorrow morning, when we will conclude. If you'd be here, please, at half past nine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 4.05 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 16th day of February, 2000, at 9.30 a.m.
